name: What if my garage was built without permits?

mainEntity.name: Can I still convert an unpermitted garage into legal living space in Los Angeles or nearby cities?
mainEntity.text: Can I still convert an unpermitted garage into legal living space in Los Angeles or nearby cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: An unpermitted garage adds risk because the project starts with a structure that may not match the records, plans, or current code requirements. Before any conversion work begins, the owner usually needs to determine what was originally permitted, what was added later, and whether the existing structure can be legalized. That can involve plan review, field verification, engineering, and corrections to electrical, framing, setbacks, or safety features. In some cases, the space can be brought into compliance and converted. In others, the cost of legalization may make the project less attractive than rebuilding or redesigning from scratch. Buyers and homeowners often underestimate how much time this adds. It is much easier to convert a garage that already has clean permits and clear history. If the garage is unpermitted, the first step is not interior design; it is document and code review. A builder should be transparent about the potential for discovery work and extra fees.
acceptedAnswer.description: An unpermitted garage can sometimes be converted, but it usually requires extra steps to verify structure, legalize existing work, and bring the space up to code. The process is often more expensive and slower than converting a fully permitted garage.
